terms.gloss: a conversation, a meeting for talks
evidence: Caes. BG 1.35, 1.43: ad colloquium vēnērunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A talk between two people, and above all a meeting between two sides to talk things over: in colloquium venīre, to come to talks. Varro defines it as people meeting in one place to talk (LL 6.57).
The ordinary word for conversation (see talk); also the dialogue of a play or of Cicero’s philosophical works, which he calls sermōnēs.

evidence: Cic. Or. 44 fin.; Brut. 60 fin.; Quint. 5.14.27 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A Greek word, used by Cicero and Quintilian of the literary form, a dialogue like Plato’s; not of everyday talks between people.

phrases.latin: in Antōniī congressum colloquiumque veniendum est
phrases.english: we have to come to a meeting and talks with Antony
